note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Louisiana switched from the November jungle primary to closed party primaries for Congress starting 2026: party primaries May 16, runoffs June 27, party nominees meet in the November general.

LA-senate.statusNote: Under Louisiana's new closed-primary system, Rep. Julia Letlow (R) faces farmer Jamie Davis (D) in November. Letlow beat state Treasurer John Fleming 57-43 and Davis beat Gary Crockett 80-20 in June 27 runoffs. Sen. Bill Cassidy, who voted to convict Trump in 2021, finished third in the May 16 GOP primary and is out.

candidates.name: Julia Letlow
candidates.background: U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 5th District since 2021 and the first Republican woman elected to Congress from Louisiana; a former university administrator with a Ph.D. in communications. She won the seat after her husband Luke died of COVID-19 before taking office. With President Trump's endorsement she defeated Sen. Bill Cassidy in the May 16 closed primary, then state Treasurer John Fleming 57-43 in the June 27 runoff.

health.label: Voted Aye on H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) with its Medicaid work requirements and spending reductions, passed 218-214 (House roll call 190, 2025)

immigration.label: Voted for H.R. 2 (Secure the Border Act of 2023), the House GOP border enforcement package, passed 219-213 (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Voted Aye on H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) extending the 2017 tax cuts, passed 218-214 (House roll call 190, 2025)

climate.label: Voted for the Lower Energy Costs Act (H.R. 1, 2023) and against the Inflation Reduction Act (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Authored the Parents Bill of Rights requiring districts to make curricula public, provide parents information on library materials, and require parental consent for school medical exams; passed the House in March 2023 (Wikipedia)

repro.label: 'I've experienced the miracle of life and will always support protecting the life of the unborn'; opposes taxpayer-funded abortion (House office)

democracy.label: Said she would have objected to the 2020 election results had she been in Congress (Wikipedia); voted Nay on the For the People Act (Ballotpedia)

sources.label: Louisiana Illuminator: Cassidy eliminated in May 16 primary

candidates.name: Jamie Davis
candidates.background: Third-generation row-crop farmer working more than 2,000 acres of cotton, corn, and soybeans in Tensas Parish; studied electrical engineering at LSU and served on the Tensas Parish Police Jury. A self-described 'country boy' and fiscal conservative running a grassroots, affordability-first campaign. Won the June 27 Democratic runoff over Gary Crockett with 80%, carrying every parish.
priorities: A farm economy that lets producers cover their bills

cost.label: Platform 'primarily focuses on an economic agenda of affordability', led by raising the federal minimum wage (Louisiana Illuminator)

health.label: Supports universal health care and 'a Medicare for all option in the future'; would reinstate ACA subsidies and reverse cuts to rural healthcare (WAFB; Louisiana Illuminator)

housing.label: Wants to 'streamline permitting for affordable housing' (Louisiana Illuminator)

immigration.label: Mixed: supports 'securing the border' while opposing an overly burdensome pathway to citizenship (WAFB)

taxes.label: Would reverse Trump tax policies 'benefitting large corporations and the wealthiest Americans'; calls himself a fiscal conservative citing $4T in added debt (Louisiana Illuminator)

repro.label: 'Men should not be making decisions about what women can do with their bodies' (WAFB)

democracy.label: Mixed: opposes restricting voter access and wants 'expanded access', but believes voters should identify themselves; backs a federal gerrymandering ban (WAFB)
